text.p: These are the leading stories in the Pakistani press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The Sindh government has opposed sacking of employees from the state-run Karachi Electric Supply Corporation saying the move would create political and social problems.

- The Federal Investigation Agency has arrested four directors and a manager of the state-run Rice Export Corporation of Pakistan on charges of alleged involvement in causing the national exchequer a loss of 160 million rupees.
- The federal government will not allow import of finished goods if trade with India is opened, a summary prepared by the Ministry of Production and Industries said.

- The reconstituted Privatisation Commission decided to complete privatisation of Sui Northern Gas Pipelines Ltd, Pakistan National Shipping Corporation, Karachi Electric Supply Corp, Habib Credit and Exchange Bank and Faisalabad Electricity Board by the end of this year.
- The federal and provincial governments are carrying a load of one million surplus staff out of a total strength of 2.2 million, according to a report prepared by the Planning Commission.
- The State (central) Bank of Pakistan is likely to announce a consolidated reform package for banking sector in the first week of May, sources said.
- The Corporate Law Commission would hold a meeting on Wednesday to review the legal framework of the Corporate Law Authority.
- The U.S.-based Mobil Corp plans to invest $10 million in the production market of downstream petroleum products in Pakistan.
- The state-run Rice Export Corporation of Pakistan has decided to invite bids again for the sale of superior quality basmati rice after rejecting the earlier offers.
- The Pakistan ambassador to Saudi Arabia has confirmed the death of 111 Pakistani pilgrims on Mina fire in Saudi Arabia.
